texts: bad: the clause has no tense marker, so it reads as a standing practice, and the two bare plurals then force the parse to invent one particular batch of letters and one particular set of villages that the sentence never claims exist; if the object instead falls back to the bare kind "letter", there is nowhere left to attach "from neighbouring villages" and the restriction is lost. Put the restricted plural in subject position so the restriction becomes part of the generalization itself: "Letters from neighbouring villages are read aloud by the Council." That version says exactly the same thing (any letter whose origin is a neighbouring village gets read aloud by the Council) while keeping the Council, the reading-aloud manner and the origin restriction all encoded, and it posits no specific letters or villages.
